# Instance

An Instance is a [SoundObject](soundobjects.qmd) on the Score that refers to a
definition in [Project SoundObjects](soundobject-library.qmd). Place the same
definition several times when a phrase or pattern should have one editable
source. Updating that source changes the material used by every linked
Instance in the project.

## Make and place Instances

Select one ordinary SoundObject on the Score and choose **Add to Project
SoundObjects** from its context menu. Blue stores the source in the project
library and replaces the selected timeline object with an Instance. For
another placement, copy and paste that Instance, or drag its definition from
**Window → Properties → Project SoundObjects** onto a SoundObject layer and
choose **Copy Instance**.

Choosing **Copy Independent** from the project library creates a new
SoundObject without the link. The user-wide [Libraries](soundobject-library.qmd)
panel also inserts independent copies. Use an independent copy if you want to
edit its content without changing the original definition or any other
placement.

## Edit source and placement

Double-click an Instance to reach the referenced object's editor. Blue marks
the properties area **Editing library object via Instance**. Changes to the
source affect all linked Instances; edit the source in **Project SoundObjects**
when you want to see that relationship clearly. You can move each Instance
to its own Score position and give it its own [Note Processor](note-processors.qmd)
chain. Those processors transform that placement's generated notes after
the shared source produces them.

For example, keep a short GenericScore phrase in Project SoundObjects, make
two Instances at different Score positions, and add an AddProcessor to one
Instance's chain. Both placements use the same source phrase, while only the
processed placement gets that added value. Inspect **Generate CSD to Screen**
to check the resulting notes.

Blue generates notes from the shared definition first, including the
definition's own Note Processors and Time Behavior. It aligns the first
generated note with the Instance's local start, runs the Instance's processor
chain, applies the Instance's Time Behavior within its Subjective Duration,
then adds the Instance's Score start offset. Set **Scale** to stretch a phrase
to the placement duration, **Repeat** to fill it with repeated notes, or
**None** to leave its length unchanged. An
Instance with an unresolved project-library reference generates no notes.
The older manual's **Convert to Generic Score** command is not present in
Blue 3; use **Copy Independent** from the project library to create an
unlinked placement.

The same placement timing applies when the shared definition generates notes
at runtime, such as a JavaScriptObject. Check **Generate CSD to Screen** when
the source script or its processors make the resulting length hard to predict.
